translation: 跳过；略过；不做（应做的事）
sub_section: Welcome to the unit
original_sentence: Carol often skips breakfast.
readingExamples: Carol often skips breakfast.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to not do something that you usually do or should do, especially eating a meal or attending a class
(2) vt. & vi. to leave out something or move past it, going on to the next thing
(3) vi. to move forward lightly and quickly, jumping from one foot to the other
(4) vt. & vi. to jump repeatedly over a rope swung under your feet

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 蹦蹦跳跳地走;轻快跳跃
uncommonMeanings.example: The little girl skipped down the lane ahead of her grandmother, her pigtails bouncing, utterly unaware that this would be the last spring they ever walked together. （读后续写·童年·温情反衬）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (不辞而别地)溜走;逃避(常 skip town / skip class)
uncommonMeanings.example: Rather than face the shame of his failing marks, he skipped class for a week, wandering the riverbank until the guilt grew heavier than any lecture could have been. （读后续写·逃避与自省）

posExamples.sentence: In her desperate rush to lose weight before the dance, Jenny began to skip breakfast day after day, never once suspecting that the very meal she scorned was the fuel her exhausted body was silently crying out for. （读后续写·健康·因小失大）
I am writing to remind every member of our study group never to skip the warm-up reading, for those few minutes lay the groundwork on which a whole productive session is built. （应用文·通知）
Those who habitually skip the small, unglamorous steps of learning often find, to their regret, that no shortcut can replace the patient labour they once thought beneath them. （议论文·勤学·反面论证）
Overjoyed at the news, the children skipped across the sunlit playground, their laughter ringing so freely that even the weary teachers paused to smile. （读后续写·喜悦·画面渲染）

idioms.translation: (心)漏跳一拍;(因紧张/激动而)心头一颤
idioms.example: When she heard her own name announced as the winner, her heart skipped a beat, and for a moment the crowded hall dissolved into a warm, dizzy blur. （读后续写·惊喜·心理描写）

collocations.example: Doctors warn that teenagers who regularly skip breakfast are far more likely to feel dizzy and lose focus long before the morning is over. （议论文·健康·数据论证）
It was only after he began to skip class that his once-brilliant marks slid, quietly and steadily, toward disaster. （读后续写·堕落·因果）
Eager to reach the exciting part, the young cook skipped a crucial step, and the cake collapsed the instant it left the oven. （读后续写·操之过急）
The examiner advised us never to skip over a difficult question in panic, but to mark it, move on, and return with a clearer mind. （应用文·经验分享）
Every evening after supper, the sisters would skip rope in the courtyard until the fireflies came out and the counting turned to giggles. （读后续写·童年·温情）
So gifted was the shy boy in mathematics that his teachers arranged for him to skip a grade, though his heart secretly ached to leave his friends behind. （读后续写·天才的孤独）
During the exam week, several devoted volunteers even skipped lunch to help set up the charity book fair on time. （应用文·活动报道）
Do not merely skip through the passage hunting for answers; a single careful reading often reveals far more than three hurried ones. （应用文·学习建议）

synonyms.example: By oversleeping just ten minutes, she missed the only bus that would have carried her to the interview of her dreams. （读后续写·错失）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:miss 强调'因故未能赶上/得到',未必是主观选择;skip 强调'主动、故意地略过或不做'该做之事

synonyms.example: In his haste, the reporter omitted one vital fact, and the whole story took on a meaning he had never intended. （议论文·媒体责任）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:omit 较正式、书面,指'省去/漏掉某部分内容';skip 更口语,常指略过步骤、章节或跳过一顿饭/一节课

synonyms.example: Determined to bypass the endless queue, the clever traveller booked her ticket online the night before. （应用文·出行建议）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:bypass 强调'绕开、避开'某障碍/环节/人;skip 强调'跳过'某步骤或不做某事,不含'迂回'之意

sub_section: Welcome to the unit

sub_section: Article: Teen faints after skipping meals
original_sentence: A teenage girl fainted yesterday at Stonechester High School after skipping meals.
readingExamples: A teenage girl fainted yesterday at Stonechester High School after skipping meals.
definitionEn:
(1) vi. to suddenly become unconscious for a short time, especially because of heat, hunger, shock or exhaustion
(2) adj. (of a sound, smell, light or feeling) not strong or clear; slight and difficult to notice
(3) adj. (of a person) feeling weak and dizzy, as if about to lose consciousness
(4) n. a sudden, brief loss of consciousness

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 微弱的,隐约的,不清晰的(声音/光线/气味/希望)
uncommonMeanings.example: Through the fog a faint light glimmered in the distance, and with it flickered the first faint hope the shipwrecked sailors had felt in days. （读后续写·绝境·一线希望）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (not have the faintest idea)一点儿也不(知道)
uncommonMeanings.example: He stared blankly at the question, not having the faintest idea where to begin, while the clock on the wall ticked mercilessly on. （读后续写·考场·慌乱）

posExamples.sentence: Halfway through the burning-hot ceremony, the exhausted girl swayed once, twice, and then fainted onto the polished floor, her collapse sending a gasp rippling through the silent hall. （读后续写·意外·紧张场面）
I am writing to warn fellow students that skipping meals to save time can make you faint in class, as one of our own classmates unfortunately did last week. （应用文·倡议书）
A faint but persistent worry gnawed at the back of my mind, warning me that something, somewhere, had gone terribly wrong. （读后续写·不祥预感）
Even the faintest act of kindness, a smile offered to a stranger, can ripple outward in ways we may never live to witness. （议论文·善意·观点论证）

wordForms.other: faint-hearted (adj. 胆怯的); faintness (n. 眩晕；微弱)

idioms.example: When the teacher asked who had left the classroom door unlocked, the whole class fell silent, for not one of them had the faintest idea. （读后续写·谜团）

idioms.idiom: faint heart never won fair lady
idioms.translation: (谚)懦夫难得美人心;不勇敢就得不到想要的
idioms.example: Reminding himself that faint heart never won fair lady, the trembling boy finally stepped forward to ask her for the very first dance. （读后续写·鼓起勇气）

collocations.translation: 因饥饿/炎热/疲惫而晕倒
collocations.example: After marching under the blazing sun for hours, several soldiers began to faint from exhaustion, one after another. （读后续写·极限考验）

In the dead of night a faint sound of footsteps reached her ears, and every hair on her arms rose in alarm. （读后续写·悬疑）
A faint smile crossed the old man's tired face, as if some long-buried happiness had briefly surfaced. （读后续写·人物神情）
Clinging to a faint hope that help might still come, the trapped miners kept tapping on the rock, hour after hour. （读后续写·绝境求生）
She grew faint with relief when the doctor at last stepped out and said, gently, that her father would be all right. （读后续写·转危为安）
He had only a faint recollection of the seaside town where, as a small boy, he had once been so happy. （读后续写·回忆）
Lost in her book, she was only faintly aware of the rain that had begun to drum softly against the window. （读后续写·氛围）

synonyms.example: The runner crossed the line, staggered two steps, and passed out into the arms of the waiting medics. （读后续写·极限）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:pass out 更口语、更强调'突然完全失去知觉倒下';faint(v.) 略正式,常暗示因虚弱/情绪等短暂晕厥,两者常可互换

synonyms.example: Overcome by grief, she collapsed onto the cold hospital chair, unable to hold herself upright a moment longer. （读后续写·悲痛）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:collapse 指'身体突然瘫软倒下',未必失去意识,程度/画面感更强;faint 特指'短暂昏厥、失去知觉'

synonyms.example: In the dim glow of the single candle, their two shadows swayed gently on the wall like old friends dancing. （读后续写·氛围）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:dim 专指光线/视线昏暗微弱;faint(adj.) 范围更广,可指声、光、味、希望等一切'微弱、隐约'之物

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. swayed once, twice, and then fainted ...
advancedExpressions.example: The exhausted messenger swayed once, twice, and then fainted at the king's very feet, the sealed letter still clutched in his whitened hand. （节奏递进+细节收束，制造戏剧性倒下）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., as one of our own classmates unfortunately did

advancedExpressions.expression: even the faintest ... can ripple outward in ways we may never ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The girl fainted because she had not eaten.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Weakened by...分词状语交代原因 + dissolve into a spinning haze 感官化描写 + before she could even cry out 时间从句制造突然感 + 三个短动词(tilted, went white, fainted)递进

sentenceUpgrade.original: There was a small hope left.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In the depths of that hopeless night, a faint hope still flickered within her, fragile as a candle flame in a gale, yet stubborn enough to keep her walking on. （读后续写·希望·比喻升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: In the depths of that hopeless night 环境铺垫 + a faint hope flickered 拟物 + fragile as a candle flame in a gale 明喻 + yet stubborn enough to... 转折强调坚持

original_sentence: She then passed out in her morning PE lesson and was rushed to hospital.

definitionEn:
(1) phr. v. to suddenly become unconscious, especially because of heat, illness, exhaustion or too much alcohol
(2) phr. v. to give something to each member of a group; to hand out or distribute
(3) phr. v. (British) to successfully complete a course of training, especially at a military or police college

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 分发,派发(给每个人)
uncommonMeanings.example: The kind-hearted teacher quietly passed out fresh copies of the notes to every student who had lost their own, asking nothing in return. （读后续写·师者·无声关怀）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (英,尤指军校/警校)结业,毕业

Scientists argue that a good night's sleep does far more than rest the body; it consolidates memory, allowing the brain to lock away what we have learned during the day. （议论文·健康）
As the fever worsened, his memory began to blur, and faces that had once been dear to him dissolved into strangers. （读后续写·疾病·心理）

wordForms.other: memo (n. 备忘录), memoir (n. 回忆录)

idioms.idiom: if my memory serves me right / correctly
idioms.example: If my memory serves me right, it was on that very bench, under the old plane tree, that we first promised to stay friends forever. （读后续写·重逢）
Flipping through the dusty photo album turned into a walk down memory lane, each faded picture unlocking a story we had almost forgotten. （读后续写·怀旧）
She committed the poem to memory not for the exam, but because its final line had spoken to something deep within her. （读后续写·成长感悟）

collocations.example: Years of irregular sleep had left him with such a poor memory that he now wrote every appointment on his palm. （读后续写·习惯后果）
The crackling of the campfire brought back memories of the summers we had spent by the lake as carefree children. （读后续写·怀旧）
Long after graduation, we would treasure the memory of those late-night talks that had shaped who we became. （应用文·毕业留言）

collocations.translation: 鲜明的 / 美好的 / 痛苦的记忆
collocations.example: Even now, decades later, the fond memory of her mother's lullaby could soothe her on the darkest of nights. （读后续写·亲情）
Studies suggest that regular exercise can boost memory and sharpen concentration far more effectively than any so-called brain pill. （议论文·健康）
No amount of time could erase the memory of the moment he let go of his father's hand in the crowded station. （读后续写·遗憾）
The scholarship was established in memory of a beloved teacher who had devoted her life to the children of the mountains. （应用文·通知）
Standing before the silent audience, she recited the entire speech from memory, her voice never once faltering. （读后续写·演讲）

synonyms.example: His recollection of that rainy afternoon remained astonishingly clear, right down to the smell of wet earth. （读后续写·回忆）
synonyms.usage: 更书面、更正式，多指对某个具体往事的回想这一动作或内容；memory 用法更广，可指记忆能力、记忆内容或计算机内存

synonyms.example: A minute of silence was observed in remembrance of those who had given their lives. （应用文·致辞）
synonyms.usage: 偏正式、庄重，多用于对逝者或重大事件的缅怀，常见于 in remembrance of；日常记忆用 memory

synonyms.example: The old sailor's reminiscences of distant ports held the children spellbound around the fire. （读后续写·长辈讲述）
synonyms.usage: 强调愉快地、深情地追述往昔，常带怀旧色彩，多用复数；memory 中性，不必然带情感

advancedExpressions.type: 读后续写·感官触发回忆
advancedExpressions.expression: the ... instantly transported sb. back to ..., a memory so vivid that ...
advancedExpressions.example: The familiar melody instantly transported her back to that snowy Christmas Eve, a memory so vivid that she could almost feel her father's coat against her cheek. （感官触发+过去场景闪回，续写回忆段）

advancedExpressions.expression: the memory of ... will forever remain etched in my heart
advancedExpressions.example: The memory of your unwavering kindness during my darkest days will forever remain etched in my heart. （感谢信情感升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: far from being a mere storehouse, memory shapes ...
advancedExpressions.example: Far from being a mere storehouse of the past, memory shapes the very identity we carry into the future, colouring every choice we make.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She remembered her grandmother's garden.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: One whiff of ripening tomatoes, and a memory long buried came rushing back: her grandmother, straw hat tilted against the sun, humming softly among the tangled vines of a garden that no longer existed. （读后续写·嗅觉+画面）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 感官触发(one whiff of) + 冒号引出画面 + 独立主格(straw hat tilted) + 定语从句收束情感(that no longer existed)

sentenceUpgrade.original: This trip gave me good memories.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: This journey has left me with memories I shall treasure for a lifetime, memories not of the sights we saw, but of the friendships that quietly took root along the way. （应用文·感谢信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 现在完成时增添分量 + memories 重复+对比结构(not of...but of...) + 隐喻(took root)

sub_section: Restrictive relative clauses with relative adverbs
original_sentence: In the long term, they may be at increased risk of having a poor memory, being overweight and suffering a heart attack.
readingExamples: In the long term, they may be at increased risk of having a poor memory, being overweight and suffering a heart attack.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a violent or aggressive act intended to hurt a person, damage a place, or defeat an enemy
(2) n. a sudden short period of illness or of a strong feeling; a fit (e.g. a heart attack, a panic attack)
(3) v. to use violence against someone or something; to try to hurt or defeat them
(4) v. to criticize someone or something strongly, in words

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （疾病的）发作
uncommonMeanings.example: Halfway up the stairs the old man clutched his chest; a heart attack, sudden and merciless, sent him crumpling to the cold marble floor. （读后续写·突发疾病·紧急救助）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 抨击，（用言语）猛烈批评
uncommonMeanings.example: The columnist fiercely attacked the new policy, arguing that it punished the very families it claimed to protect. （议论文·社会评论）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 着手处理（难题、任务）
uncommonMeanings.example: Rolling up his sleeves, he attacked the mountain of overdue homework with a determination that surprised even himself. （读后续写·学业态度）

posExamples.sentence: Out of nowhere a panic attack seized her; her heart hammered, her palms turned to ice, and the crowded hall seemed to close in around her. （读后续写·心理·焦虑发作）
The stray dog, cornered and terrified, suddenly attacked the boy who had only meant to help it. （读后续写·意外冲突）
I am writing to warn residents that thieves tend to attack when the streets are quiet, so please keep your doors locked after dark. （应用文·公告/提醒）
Rather than attacking those who disagree with us, we should learn to challenge their ideas with reason and respect. （议论文·理性讨论）

idioms.example: For proposing longer study hours, the headmaster soon came under attack from students and parents alike. （议论文·争议话题）

idioms.idiom: attack is the best form of defence
idioms.example: Believing that attack is the best form of defence, the young debater opened not by shielding her own view but by dismantling her rival's. （读后续写·辩论）

collocations.example: Under cover of darkness the raiders launched an attack on the sleeping camp. （读后续写·冒险）
The shocking news was so overwhelming that his grandfather very nearly had a heart attack. （读后续写·突发事件）
The thick smoke triggered an asthma attack, and she fought desperately for every breath. （读后续写·危急时刻）
The reform came under fierce attack from those who feared losing their long-held privileges. （议论文·社会）
The essay was widely read as a bold attack on the culture of overwork poisoning modern schools. （议论文·社会评论）
Clutching a broken oar, the fisherman fought to fend off the shark's relentless attack. （读后续写·海上求生）
She attacked the coding challenge line by line, refusing to give up until every bug was gone. （读后续写·钻研精神）
Instead of verbally attacking his opponent, the captain calmly presented the facts and let them speak for themselves. （议论文·理性）

synonyms.example: The sudden assault left the guard reeling, and the alarm shattered the silence of the night. （读后续写·冲突）
synonyms.usage: 更强调猛烈、突然的人身或军事袭击，语气比 attack 更重，也是法律术语（人身伤害罪）；attack 用法更宽，可指言语、疾病、任务等

synonyms.example: The editorial criticized the plan for ignoring the needs of rural students. （议论文·评论）
synonyms.usage: 仅指言语上的批评，中性偏客观；attack 表示批评时语气更激烈、带敌意

synonyms.example: The team met at dawn to tackle the flooding before it reached the village. （应用文·报道）
synonyms.usage: 指积极着手解决问题或任务，语气中性积极；attack 表此义时更强调猛烈、全力以赴的劲头

advancedExpressions.expression: without warning, ... attacked / an attack seized sb.
advancedExpressions.example: Without warning, a wave of dizziness attacked her, and the world tilted violently beneath her feet. （突发危机+身体反应，续写高潮段）

advancedExpressions.expression: to guard against ..., we are advised to ...
advancedExpressions.example: To guard against sudden attacks by stray animals, we are strongly advised to walk in groups after dusk. （公告结尾建议）

advancedExpressions.expression: instead of attacking ..., we ought to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Instead of attacking those whose opinions differ from ours, we ought to engage them in reasoned dialogue, for truth is refined, not destroyed, by disagreement.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The dog attacked him and he was scared.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Before he could even cry out, the dog lunged and attacked, its bared teeth flashing white in the fading light, and a cold wave of terror surged through every fibre of his body. （读后续写·动作+恐惧）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: before 时间状语制造紧迫 + 动词升级(lunged and attacked) + 细节(bared teeth flashing white) + 心理描写(cold wave of terror surged)

sentenceUpgrade.original: People attacked the new rule.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: No sooner had the new rule been announced than it came under fierce attack, with parents and teachers alike condemning it as hasty, ill-considered and blind to the realities of student life. （议论文·社会评论）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: No sooner...than 倒装制造张力 + 被动 came under attack + with 复合结构 + 三形容词递进(hasty, ill-considered, blind)

sub_section: Restrictive relative clauses with relative adverbs
original_sentence: Everyone knows that the amount of quality sleep we get is important to us.
readingExamples: Everyone knows that the amount of quality sleep we get is important to us.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a quantity of something, especially the total quantity of money, time or a substance
(2) n. a sum of money
(3) v. (amount to) to add up to a total; to be equal to a particular figure
(4) v. (amount to) to be the same as something, or to have the same effect as it

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （amount to）等同于，无异于
uncommonMeanings.example: His stubborn silence at that crucial moment amounted to a confession, and everyone in the room knew it. （读后续写·真相揭露）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （amount to）（数量）加起来达到，总计
uncommonMeanings.example: By the end of the charity sale, the coins the children had gathered amounted to more than a thousand yuan. （应用文·活动报道）

posExamples.sentence: No amount of apology could undo the hurt his careless words had caused, yet he swallowed his pride and tried all the same. （读后续写·和解）
I am writing to report that, thanks to your generosity, a considerable amount of money has been raised for the flood-stricken families. （应用文·感谢信）
The amount of pressure heaped upon today's teenagers, some argue, is quietly robbing them of the very childhood that should shape them. （议论文·教育）
Ignoring the drowning stranger, the onlookers eventually realised, would amount to a betrayal of everything they claimed to believe. （读后续写·道德抉择）

idioms.example: No amount of money could ever buy back the years he had spent chasing wealth instead of his children's laughter. （读后续写·顿悟）

idioms.idiom: amount to nothing / not amount to much
idioms.translation: 毫无结果，成不了什么气候
idioms.example: They had told him his dreams would amount to nothing, yet years later his invention was changing lives across the country. （读后续写·励志）

collocations.phrase: a large / small / huge amount of
collocations.translation: 大量的 / 少量的（不可数）
collocations.example: A huge amount of effort had gone into the surprise party, and her tears made every sleepless hour worthwhile. （读后续写·感动）

collocations.phrase: the amount of + 不可数名词
collocations.example: Everyone knows that the amount of quality sleep we get shapes how sharply we think the next day. （议论文·健康）
A certain amount of nervousness before a speech is not a weakness but a sign that you truly care. （应用文·经验分享）
The total amount donated exceeded our wildest hopes, and the whole class erupted into cheers. （应用文·活动报道）
To protect our oceans, each of us must reduce the amount of plastic we throw away every single day. （议论文·环保）
The repairs amounted to nearly ten thousand yuan, a sum the young couple could scarcely afford. （读后续写·生活压力）
No amount of persuasion could shake her quiet resolve to become a doctor. （读后续写·坚定）

collocations.phrase: an enormous / considerable amount of time
collocations.example: She had poured a considerable amount of time into rehearsing, and it showed in every confident gesture. （读后续写·付出）

synonyms.example: A small quantity of salt is enough to transform the whole dish. （说明文·生活）
synonyms.usage: 较中性、正式，可搭配可数或不可数名词，强调可测量的多少；amount 通常只接不可数名词，且常与金钱、时间、努力等抽象量搭配

synonyms.example: A growing number of students now choose to study abroad after graduation. （议论文·教育）
synonyms.usage: 只用于可数名词(the number of students)；amount 用于不可数名词(the amount of water)，二者切勿混用

synonyms.example: He donated a generous sum to rebuild the village school. （应用文·报道）
synonyms.usage: 特指一笔具体的钱款；amount 泛指数量，用于金钱时侧重总量而非单笔

advancedExpressions.expression: no amount of ... could ...
advancedExpressions.example: No amount of time or distance could dim the memory of that final embrace on the platform. （否定强调+情感，续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.expression: even the smallest amount of ... can make a difference
advancedExpressions.example: Even the smallest amount of your support can make a real difference to a child who has never owned a single book. （呼吁信打动读者）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is not the amount of ... but the quality of ... that ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is not the amount of time we spend studying but the quality of our focus that truly determines success.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She tried a lot but nothing worked.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: No amount of coaxing, no amount of promises, could persuade the frightened child to loosen his grip on the railing. （读后续写·僵持场面）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: No amount of...重复排比强化 + 具体名词(coaxing, promises) + 画面细节(loosen his grip on the railing)

sentenceUpgrade.original: We raised a lot of money.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I am delighted to report that, through everyone's tireless effort, the amount we raised far surpassed our initial target, bringing warmth to dozens of families this winter. （应用文·感谢信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: I am delighted to report that 应用文套语 + through 状语点明原因 + 结果 far surpassed our target + 分词收束意义(bringing warmth)

sub_section: Restrictive relative clauses with relative adverbs
original_sentence: Try to stick to your sleep schedule at the weekend too, even though weekends are probably the time when you feel like a lie-in.
readingExamples: Try to stick to your sleep schedule at the weekend too, even though weekends are probably the time when you feel like a lie-in.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a plan that lists all the work that you have to do and when you must do each thing; a timetable
(2) n. a list of the times when trains, buses, planes, etc. arrive and depart
(3) v. to arrange for something to happen or take place at a particular time
(4) n. a formal list, especially an official list of prices, rates or conditions attached to a document

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 安排，将……列入计划（在某时间发生）
uncommonMeanings.example: The surgery had been scheduled for dawn, and as the hours crept by, the family sat clutching one another in the pale hospital light. （读后续写·手术等待·焦灼）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （火车、公交、航班的）时刻表
uncommonMeanings.example: A single glance at the departure schedule told her the last train home had already left the platform. （读后续写·错过·失落）

posExamples.sentence: Try to stick to your sleep schedule at the weekend too, for the body, like a loyal clock, quietly rewards those who keep their promises to it. （议论文·健康）
I am writing to enclose a detailed schedule for the upcoming charity week, so that every volunteer knows exactly where and when to lend a hand. （应用文·通知）
The interview had been scheduled for nine, yet by half past he was still pacing the corridor, rehearsing his answers under his breath. （读后续写·面试·紧张）
A punishing schedule of extra classes, some educators warn, leaves students too exhausted to think, let alone to dream. （议论文·教育）

idioms.example: Working through the night, the volunteers finished the whole mural a full day ahead of schedule. （读后续写·集体努力）
Despite the storm, the relief supplies arrived right on schedule, and a cheer rose from the waiting crowd. （读后续写·希望）
However tight her schedule, she always found ten quiet minutes to write to her grandmother. （读后续写·亲情）

collocations.example: Sticking to a strict revision schedule turned the chaos of exam week into something she could finally control. （读后续写·自律）
Between training and studying, his packed schedule left barely a moment to breathe. （读后续写·压力）

collocations.translation: 睡眠 / 工作 / 训练时间表
collocations.example: Doctors recommend keeping a regular sleep schedule, even at the weekend, to protect the body's natural rhythm. （议论文·健康）

collocations.translation: 提前 / 落后 / 准时
collocations.example: Thanks to everyone's dedication, the project was completed two weeks ahead of schedule. （应用文·报道）
Before the trip, we drew up a careful schedule so that no one would be left standing at the wrong gate. （应用文·计划）
Somehow she managed to fit weekly hospital visits into her already overflowing schedule. （读后续写·善良）
The rehearsal has been scheduled for four o'clock, so please do not be late. （应用文·通知）
Beneath his hectic schedule lay a quiet fear that if he ever stopped moving, the loneliness would catch up with him. （读后续写·心理）

synonyms.example: The new timetable squeezed three science lessons into a single gruelling afternoon. （应用文·校园）
synonyms.usage: 英式英语常用，多指课程表、火车时刻表等固定重复的安排；schedule 更宽泛，可指个人日程、工作计划，也可作动词

synonyms.example: Their plan for the weekend fell apart the moment the rain began. （读后续写·意外）
synonyms.usage: 泛指对未来行动的打算，不必然含精确时间；schedule 强调按具体时间点排定的安排

synonyms.example: Climate change now sits at the very top of the world's agenda. （议论文·社会）
synonyms.usage: 多指会议议程或需处理事项的清单，也可引申为优先要务；schedule 侧重按时间排定的活动安排

advancedExpressions.expression: however carefully sb. had planned the schedule, ...
advancedExpressions.example: However carefully she had planned every hour of the schedule, one phone call was enough to send it all crashing down. （让步+突转，续写转折段）

advancedExpressions.expression: please find enclosed a detailed schedule of ...
advancedExpressions.example: Please find enclosed a detailed schedule of the exchange programme, so that participants may prepare accordingly. （通知正文引出附件）

advancedExpressions.expression: a well-ordered schedule is not a cage but a compass
advancedExpressions.example: A well-ordered schedule is not a cage that confines us but a compass that frees us to pursue what truly matters.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She had a busy schedule but still helped others.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: However crowded her schedule grew, she never once turned away a classmate in need, always squeezing out a spare half-hour as if kindness itself kept perfect time. （读后续写·品格）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: However 让步从句 + never once 强调 + 分词状语(always squeezing out) + 明喻(as if kindness kept perfect time)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Here is the plan for the event.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: To ensure that the event runs smoothly, I have drawn up a detailed schedule below, setting out the time, venue and person in charge for each activity. （应用文·通知）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: To ensure 目的状语开头 + 完成时 have drawn up + 分词补充说明(setting out the time, venue...) 三项并列清晰

sub_section: Restrictive relative clauses with relative adverbs
original_sentence: These negative thoughts are one reason why you stay awake after the light goes off.
readingExamples: These negative thoughts are one reason why you stay awake after the light goes off.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. harmful, unpleasant, or not wanted; bad
(2) adj. considering only the bad side of something or someone; lacking enthusiasm or hope; pessimistic
(3) adj. expressing 'no'; showing refusal, denial or the absence of something
(4) adj. (of a medical or scientific test) showing that a substance or condition is not present
(5) n. a word or statement that means 'no' or expresses denial

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （医学检测）阴性的
uncommonMeanings.example: When the doctor announced that the test had come back negative, the whole family let out a breath they had been holding for days. （读后续写·如释重负）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （摄影）底片；负数；否定词
uncommonMeanings.example: In the dim red glow of the darkroom, he held the negative up to the light and watched the forgotten summer slowly reappear. （读后续写·旧照片·怀旧）

posExamples.sentence: These negative thoughts wrapped around her like a fog, and the harder she tried to sleep, the more wide awake she became. （读后续写·失眠·心理）
I am writing to express my concern about the negative effects that excessive screen time is having on our classmates' eyesight and mood. （应用文·建议信）
Dwelling on the negative aspects of failure, some argue, blinds us to the priceless lessons that only setbacks can teach. （议论文·成长）
His reply was curt and negative, and with a single shake of the head he crushed the small hope she had dared to nurse. （读后续写·失望）

collocations.phrase: a negative effect / impact / influence on
collocations.example: Staying up late scrolling through videos has a startling negative effect on both memory and mood. （议论文·健康）
She learned to greet her negative thoughts like passing clouds, neither fighting them nor letting them stay. （读后续写·心理成长）
A negative attitude, his coach warned, would defeat him long before any opponent ever could. （读后续写·励志）
Rather than being crushed by the negative feedback, she read it twice and turned every criticism into a plan for improvement. （读后续写·成长）
When the audience reacted negatively, the young speaker paused, breathed, and won them back with a single honest smile. （读后续写·演讲）
To everyone's relief, all the passengers eventually tested negative and were allowed to go home. （应用文·报道）
The media too often portrays teenagers in a negative light, ignoring the countless quiet acts of kindness they perform. （议论文·社会）
Ignoring the warning signs of exhaustion can lead to negative consequences that no amount of coffee will fix. （议论文·健康）

synonyms.example: Even in the bleakest weeks, she refused to become pessimistic, insisting that a door would open if she kept knocking. （读后续写·乐观）
synonyms.usage: 专指对未来悲观、总预期坏结果的心态；negative 含义更广，可指有害的、否定的、阴性的等

synonyms.example: Excessive noise is far more harmful to concentration than most students realise. （议论文·健康）
synonyms.usage: 直接强调造成实际伤害或损害；negative 常指影响不好、令人不快，程度不一定到伤害

synonyms.example: Despite the unfavourable weather, the whole team turned up for the charity run. （应用文·报道）
synonyms.usage: 较正式，指不利的条件或不赞成的态度；negative 更口语常用，且可指情绪、检测结果等

advancedExpressions.expression: she brushed the negative thoughts aside and ...
advancedExpressions.example: Taking a deep breath, she brushed the negative thoughts aside and let a fragile spark of hope take their place. （动作+心理转折，续写由暗转明）

advancedExpressions.expression: in view of the negative effects of ..., I would suggest that ...

advancedExpressions.expression: what appears negative at first glance may prove ...
advancedExpressions.example: What appears negative at first glance — a harsh critique, a painful loss — may prove, in time, the very force that reshapes us for the better.

sentenceUpgrade.original: He had negative thoughts and could not sleep.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Long after the light went off, negative thoughts circled his mind like restless moths around a lamp, and sleep, however desperately he chased it, slipped further and further away. （读后续写·失眠·心理）

sub_section: Article: Don't judge a book by its cover
original_sentence: Teens who try to copy the looks of their favourite stars are fighting a losing battle—these standards are simply impossible for most of the population to live up to.

synonyms.translation: 艰苦的斗争，困难重重之事

sub_section: Article: Don't judge a book by its cover

definitionEn:
